newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro will come on time, fulfilling criteria - Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Euro will come on time, fulfilling criteria - Kohl.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday there was no doubt Europe needed a single currency and vowed to do all he could to ensure it would arrive on time, saying a delay would not solve current problems in Germany.

Kohl told the Bundestag lower house of parliament there would be no softening of the Maastricht criteria to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU) and that a delay in the planned 1999 launch would cause havoc in financial markets.

The German government retreated on a plan to revalue Bundesbank assets after a meeting between Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday. The government had intended to help plug yawning budget gaps in order to qualify for EMU this year

Bonn's abandonment of Waigel's plan, which the opposition and the press called an embarassing climbdown, made Germany's chances of fulfilling the Maastricht criteria seem distant. But Kohl said he was confident Germany would manage this.

"A delay would have an enormous impact on financial markets and the German economy's chances in the export market," Kohl said. "The German government will keep firmly to the timetable and criteria for currency union."
Germany and other nations that hope to join EMU are struggling to reduce their public debt and deficits to target levels in 1997.
